svg.title: Dijkstra's Shortest Path
svg.desc: Dijkstra's Shortest Path. Settle the closest unsettled node, relax its edges, repeat: shortest paths from one source when no edge weight is negative. Step 1, Tentative distances: A starts at 0 and every other node at ∞. Settle A and relax its edges: B gets 4, C gets 1. Step 2, Settle the closest: Pop the smallest, C = 1: no other route can be shorter. C cuts B to 3; B settles and cuts D to 4. Step 3, Repeat, then read paths: Skip stale entries, settle D, E and F; prev links from F trace A→C→B→D→E→F = 8, not A→B→D→F = 11. Step 4, No negative edges: With a negative edge, A settles at 2 though S → B → A costs only 1: use Bellman–Ford instead.

g.text: A starts at 0 and every other node at ∞. Settle A and relax its edges: B gets 4, C gets 1.
Pop the smallest, C = 1: no other route can be shorter. C cuts B to 3; B settles and cuts D to 4.
Skip stale entries, settle D, E and F; prev links from F trace A→C→B→D→E→F = 8, not A→B→D→F = 11.
With a negative edge, A settles at 2 though S → B → A costs only 1: use Bellman–Ford instead.
relax u–v: is d[u] + w < d[v]?
d[A] = 0, every other d = ∞; push (0, A)
final: other routes start with A–B = 4
the old (4, B) stays in the queue
pop (4, B): B is settled at 3, skip
pop (6, D): D is settled at 4, skip
A → C → B → D → E → F = 8
O((V + E) log V) with a binary heap
O(V²) with an array: for dense graphs
